gap: No result ChatGPT got states that on 2026-11-17 the cheapest 1 kWh power stations rated for a 10 ms switchover cost less than the 20 ms BLUETTI AC180 at the maker stores: the EcoFlow DELTA 3 Classic is $459, the BLUETTI Elite 100 V2 is $499 and the AC180 is $549.
standout_why: ChatGPT ran no searches and got no results, so there are no rival pages to compare against. Its answer named no models and no prices. It only said to look for 10 ms or less and to prefer a dedicated UPS. StorageReview's test, which our current page cites, has measured times for six older stations, but its PC was idle and it gives no prices. Neither source matches today's prices to rated switchover times. Our own page also leaves out two models: the Elite 100 V2, which we list through awin:bluetti_us, and the DELTA 3 Classic.
decides: The finding removes the BLUETTI AC180 as a pick. At $549 it costs $50 more than BLUETTI's own Elite 100 V2 ($499), and it is rated 20 ms against 10 ms with the same 1,800 W output. The value pick for a gaming PC becomes the Elite 100 V2 or the DELTA 3 Classic ($459). The DELTA 3 Plus ($649) stays the pick if the shopper wants EcoFlow's USB UPS data link. The Elite 200 V2 ($899) and Elite 300 ($1,199) are the long-outage picks. Every 10 ms figure here is the maker's rating, not a measurement. StorageReview tested with the PC idle, so no source here shows any of these stations holding up a PC under gaming load.

findings.source_title: EcoFlow DELTA 3 Classic Portable Power Station (1024Wh)
findings.note: Read with storecheck from the Shopify product data. The listing text says '10ms Auto-Switch', 1,800 W output (3,600 W surge) and 1,024 Wh. This is the lowest price for a 10 ms-rated 1 kWh station in this sweep. It loses where you need a PC shutdown signal: the listing mentions no USB UPS data link.
